name: Taller de Gráfica Popular linocut
summary: A black-and-white print cut in linoleum or wood. The Taller de Gráfica Popular made leaflets, posters and portfolios for workers, unions and the state, in large black masses and white gouge lines.

philosophy.core_thesis: A print that a collective cuts quickly in cheap material can serve a political cause and reach a wide public.
design_principles: Cut the block with a gouge, so that the white line stays bold and clear.
Fill the picture with solid black and let the white line draw the form.
Show workers, peasants and soldiers in a strong action, drawn from a low or a close view.
Add hand-lettered text: a slogan, a name or a verse.
Print in black; add a red block only where the message needs it.
Print on cheap paper in editions of tens to thousands.
Make work with the group: one artist cuts, others print and share the plate.
anti_patterns: A neutral message with no stand
Pale, thin line work that the press cannot hold

process.matrix: A block of linoleum or wood.
process.press: Hand burnishing with a spoon or a small press; a litho press for large sheets.
process.image_making: The artist cuts the white areas with a gouge and leaves the black as raised surface.
process.edition: Tens to thousands of sheets; the block holds well.

inks.strategy: One black ink, with a second block in red for some sheets.

screening.rule: Make a tone only with the width and the spacing of gouge lines, 0.3–1.5 mm apart; do not use a screen.

registration.rule: Register a second block with pin marks; a shift of up to 1 mm is normal in a hand-printed edition.

substrate.stock: A cheap offset paper or a thin Japanese paper.

surface.impression: A light to medium bite, deeper in the burnished black areas.
surface.sheen: Matt black with a slight shine on thick ink.
surface.texture: Solid black with a mottled speckle, gouge strokes and a ragged edge.

positive: bold gouged white lines on black

evidence.title: Broadsheet: the ballad of Mr Grasshopper at communion
evidence.maker: Taller de Gráfica Popular, after Leopoldo Méndez
evidence.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (46.46.459) via Wikimedia Commons. Photo-relief and letterpress on green paper, c.1940.

evidence.title: Flyer on profiteers who exploit farmworkers (ladder of profiteers)
evidence.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art via Wikimedia Commons. Photo-relief and letterpress, c.1936–1945.

emotion.target_response: Solidarity and anger: the viewer feels a strong, plain and human call to act.

avoid_when: The brand needs a neutral, polished or luxury tone.
The image needs fine tone or a photographic likeness.

modifiers.how: Replace the heroic figure with a skeleton, add cross-hatch and a short verse in type.
Replace the heavy black masses with parallel shading lines and print on laid paper.
